column1: # B1183 (#502) legH: the LOOT row, with the corpse held long enough and
# placed IN FRONT of the caster's camera.
# Why legG failed (measured, B1183 legG FINDINGS): #spawn puts the TrollF at
# the caster's own position -- directly under the third-person camera -- so
# its corpse is at/below the screen bottom and the (640,430) click hit
# nothing (22_kill frame: empty foreground, target frame stuck on the caster).
# This leg (1) holds the corpse via the server-SQL hook (EmptyNPCCorpseDecayTime
# 0 -> 300000, so it does not despawn ~1.03 s after OP_Death) and (2) moves the
# caster 3 units to -Y with heading 0 (EQ heading 0 = +Y/North, docs/CLAUDE.md
# "Heading/Rotation Conventions"), so the corpse (at +Y) is in front and large.
# The oracle writes 105 to the CORPSE's +0x251 (loot gate 28061/28062), not the
# looter's -- the poller's XNEW/XWR lines (non-local spawns) carry the corpse,
# the WR lines carry the looter (should hold 100).
# B1192 (#511): B1183 wrote this file SPACE-delimited; the session's
# `awk -F'\t' '$1=="login"'` (oracle_session.sh) found no login row, so
# CHARACTER was empty and legH3 died at the (then-silent) account_id check.
# This file is the same plan with real tabs.
# B1192 (run 2, 2026-10-29): B1183's plan was ALSO missing the two observer
# directives the `obs` rows require -- `# observer=<Character>` (the
# session/remote parse it from the plan; oracle_session.sh:266,
# oracle_remote.sh:876) and `# obs-ini-set=Defaults.LastCharSel=1` (the
# observer account holds two characters, Darkshadow slot 0 / Oraclewatch
# slot 1; without it `obs zone` clicks slot 0 and the WRONG character
# enters). Without `# observer=`, every obs row died at
# oracle_remote.sh's `[[ -n $OBSERVER ]] || exit 65` -- again silently
# (empty remote.log, timeline stuck at 01_char_select). Run 2 measured
# exactly that; the session now refuses the shape before the client
# (oracle_session.sh, B1192 guard). Both directives are added below, in
# B1176's canonical form (refactor/B1176/leg/o_human.tsv:32-38).
# B1192 v3 (run 7, 2026-10-29): run 6's /loot never opened the loot window
# (no loot/target packet at loot_open, corpse byte held 120 -- poll.log,
# 29_use_check.png: target frame still on Oraclewatch). The v3 claim that
# the official client has no name-based corpse targeting is RETRACTED:
# run 9's post-kill /target TrollF (37_retarget) resolved the corpse,
# OP_TargetCommand target=260 was server-acknowledged, and /loot opened
# the loot window (refactor/B1192/README.md, measured row). Run 6's
# /target TrollF set the live troll BEFORE death, with no post-kill retarget;
# OP_Death cleared HoTT (XCORPSE at t=5.559, poll.log),
# and the loot gate (decompile 18431: DAT_00905d04 = the corpse getter,
# case '\x06': corpse must exist and +0x244 == 0) found no corpse target.
# The poller's dec_slot had ALSO mis-decoded the keymap (it read the
# keycode as low bits + modifier flags; the real encoding is the keycode
# in the HIGH byte: run-6 SLOT 24 raw 0x3b000000 = F1 = TARGETME, 29 =
# F6, 30 = F7 TARGETPC, 32 = F8 TARGETNPC -- the official bindings). v3:
#   - #corpse deleteplayercorpses (eqemu zone/gm_commands/corpse.cpp:
#     entity_list.DeletePlayerCorpses, "all player corpses") clears the
#     stale Oraclewatch PC corpse (visible in every still, outside the
#     spawn list the poller walks) so the scene holds exactly one corpse;
#   - the troll is killed back-to-back with no settle waits (run 6 gave it
#     5.5 s of AI: 19_spawn -> 23_kill), so its corpse lands at the spawn
#     point, in front of the camera;
#   - the corpse is TARGETED after the kill: press F8 (TARGETNPC = nearest
#     NPC in field of view; dead included -- the live keymap binds action
#     32 to F8, run-6 poll.log KEYMAP 0x080:1107296256 = 0x42000000) with
#     a click on the corpse blob as corrector (if F8 already set the
#     target the click re-targets the same corpse; a ground miss walks the
#     caster the remaining 1-2 units toward it, shortening the loot range);
#   - the caster poses at (-76,425): the corpse (-77,428) is 3.2 units
#     ahead-left, inside the loot range and the field of view.
# B1192 v4 (run 8, 2026-10-29): run 7's click (405,700) hit the corpse
# (OP_TargetMouse target=268 -> OP_LootRequest); run 8's identical click at
# the identical geometry (scene pixels unchanged, only the right-hand UI
# bars differ -- the diff bbox is x>=421) produced NO TargetMouse at all,
# so /loot saw the F8 target (NPC 31) and did nothing: the corpse-blob
# raycast is a coin flip at this size/distance, and F8 always picks the
# closer LIVE NPC 31. v4 makes the corpse the LAST word: a 3-point click
# sweep around the proven point (misses keep the previous target, so the
# sweep can only add the corpse, never remove it), then `/target TrollF`
# AFTER the kill -- the corpse keeps its name prefix (TrollF ->
# TrollF`s_corpseNNN, poll.log) and /target resolves names to spawn ids
# server-acknowledged (step 25: OP_TargetCommand target=260) -- so if the
# name lookup includes corpses the target is deterministic and geometry-free,
# and if it doesn't, the sweep's best result stands. F8 is gone: it always
# overwrites a good corpse target with NPC 31.
